what_is_canton.title: What is Canton Network?
what_is_canton.summary: Privacy-enabled blockchain for institutional use. Apps use the Canton ledger for multi-org business processes with automatic state sync and privacy. Apps compose on-ledger (atomic Daml transactions) and off-ledger (APIs). Used by Hashnote, Brale, SocGen for tokenized RWAs.
key_points: Multi-party apps with automatic state synchronization
Privacy by design — data only shared with relevant parties
Not all apps need custom Daml — can build on other apps' code or APIs
Complementary to public blockchains — institutional privacy use cases

privacy_model.title: Canton Privacy Model
privacy_model.summary: Selective visibility — participants only see transactions they're party to. NO shared global state. Synchronizer nodes CANNOT decrypt payloads.
key_points: Principle 1: Parties see actions they have a stake in
Principle 2: Every party seeing an action sees its transitive consequences
Synchronizer only sees encrypted envelopes and routing metadata
Data minimization on need-to-know basis

daml_language.title: Daml Smart Contract Language
daml_language.summary: Functional smart contract language. Templates = classes, contracts = objects, choices = methods. Compiled to Daml-LF bytecode, packaged as DAR files.
key_points: template: contract schema. 'with' block for fields, 'where' block for logic
signatory: parties required to create/archive. Every contract needs at least one
observer: parties who can see but not act. Guaranteed to see create/archive
choice: permissioned function. controller specifies who can exercise
nonconsuming: choice that doesn't archive the contract
ensure: template precondition (Bool). e.g. ensure amount > 0.0
assert/assertMsg: runtime checks in choices
Error handling: prefer failWithStatus over exceptions — protocol version 35 has no rollback nodes
Daml Script: testing. allocateParty, submit, createCmd, exerciseCmd, submitMustFail
daml.yaml: project config. Always include daml-prim, daml-stdlib in dependencies
DAR file: compiled artifact in .daml/dist/. Self-contained like a JAR
Package hash: the ONLY reliable identifier for deployed packages (hex string)

party_id.title: Party IDs
party_id.summary: NOT like ETH addresses. Cannot generate locally — need a participant node. Format: name::fingerprint. Use parties economically.
key_points: Format: <hint>::<namespace_fingerprint> e.g. alice::12200b11a778...
Party Name: max 185 chars [a-zA-Z0-9_], unique in namespace
Fingerprint: from validator's key (internal) or external signing key
Allocate via Admin API or JSON Ledger API POST /v2/parties
External parties retain own signing keys for security
Avoid ephemeral parties — one party per wallet/account

cip_0103_standard.title: CIP-0103 — Canton dApp Standard
cip_0103_standard.summary: The wallet-to-dApp connectivity standard for Canton. Analogous to WalletConnect / EIP-1193 on Ethereum. Any wallet implementing the dApp API and any dApp using the dApp SDK are automatically interoperable — no bespoke per-pair integration needed.
key_points: Solves the N×M integration problem: N wallets × M dApps would require N×M custom integrations without the standard
Wallets implement the dApp API (server or browser extension)
dApps consume the dApp SDK and embed the Discovery Component
Supports both sync flows (browser extensions) and async flows (server-side / mobile)
Canton-specific: the connection includes party identity and validator node context — not just an address
Discovery Component = RainbowKit equivalent for Canton
Implemented and maintained by Digital Asset Wallet Unit

wallet_unit_products.title: DA Wallet Unit — Product Suite
wallet_unit_products.summary: Six products from Digital Asset's Wallet Unit that form the wallet and application connectivity layer for Canton Network. Built on open-source, provider-agnostic, institutional-ready principles.

products.wallet_sdk: TypeScript SDK for institutions/exchanges/custodians. Wraps Ledger API. Handles party creation, tx submission, delegations, balance queries.
products.dapp_sdk: CIP-0103 implementation for dApp developers. App-side of the wallet-dApp handshake. Sync + async wallet support.
products.discovery_component: Drop-in UI widget. Shows available CIP-0103 wallets for user to connect. Pairs with dApp SDK. Always include both.
products.wallet_gateway: Deployed by validators/institutions. Bridges validator node to external custody (Fireblocks, BitGo, DFNS, Blockdaemon) via signing drivers. Keys never leave custody.
products.reference_wallet: Open-source production browser extension wallet. Real key management, real signing, CIP-0103 compliant. No validator bundled — users need their own node access.
products.portfolio_ui: Open-source dApp dashboard. View holdings, offers, allocations. NOT a wallet. Connects via CIP-0103. Replaces splice amulet wallet UI over time.

wallet_unit_products.unifyingStandard: CIP-0103 — all six products are designed around it
key_points: Wallet SDK + Wallet Gateway often used together by institutional validators
dApp SDK + Discovery Component always shipped together
Reference Wallet dogfoods the SDK/standard and serves as reference for external wallet teams
Portfolio UI is end-user facing and works with any CIP-0103 wallet including Wallet Gateway setups

synchronizer.title: Synchronizer
synchronizer.summary: Provides sequencing (ordered encrypted communication) and mediation (two-phase commit). NOT a validator.
key_points: Sequencer: ordered, encrypted message delivery
Mediator: aggregates confirmations, approves/rejects transactions
Global Synchronizer: shared synchronizer for Canton Network
Cannot decrypt payloads — privacy by design
Ordering layer is moving from CometBFT to CantonBFT — see CONCEPTS.cantonbft

cantonbft.title: CantonBFT (ordering layer)
cantonbft.summary: CantonBFT (formerly DA BFT) is a tailor-made BFT ordering service for Canton. It replaces the single-leader CometBFT ordering service with a parallel, multi-leader consensus protocol for higher throughput and better availability with slow or faulty peers.
key_points: GA for private synchronizers since Canton 3.5.15 (2026-08-27)
Global Synchronizer: Splice 0.8.0 prepared the ordering layer for the CometBFT → CantonBFT switch; the switch requires an LSU
The switch LSU has already happened on DevNet; TestNet/MainNet rollout to be announced
Canton 3.5.16–3.5.18 are largely CantonBFT stability and performance releases

logical_synchronizer_upgrades.title: Logical Synchronizer Upgrades (LSU, CIP-0117)
logical_synchronizer_upgrades.summary: LSU upgrades the synchronizer (protocol version, ordering layer, disaster recovery) without a hard migration. Since Splice 0.6.2 it is the ONLY supported mechanism; Hard Domain Migrations are gone.
key_points: MIGRATION_ID is frozen — validators keep their current value for the foreseeable future
SVs use a SERIAL_ID that increments with each LSU for synchronizer node naming
Validators must run Splice 0.6.5+ before any LSU or they cannot submit/receive transactions until they upgrade
Roll-forward LSUs are used for network-wide disaster recovery
Canton 3.5.18 ensures nodes can process an LSU announcement to protocol version 36
Scan internal API /v0/lsu exposes topology freeze time, upgrade time and successor synchronizer ID

utxo_model.title: UTXO Model
utxo_model.summary: Each Daml contract = one UTXO. Distributed only to stakeholder nodes.
key_points: 1:1 correspondence: Daml contract = UTXO
Active Contract Set (ACS) = unspent outputs for a party
Contracts immutable — update by archive old + create new
All transactions atomic — commit fully or fail

transaction_model.title: Transaction Model
transaction_model.summary: Transactions are atomic trees of actions. Requester knows all consequences — no surprises.
key_points: Steps: interpret → blind → submit → validate → commit → confirm → complete
All transactions atomic
Required authorizers: create=signatories, exercise=controllers, archive=signatories
Authorization rule: required authorizers ⊆ parent transaction's authorizers

token_standard.title: Token Standard (CIP-0056)
token_standard.summary: Standard APIs for Canton tokens. Inspired by ERC20 but for UTXO model with privacy. CC implements the full standard. V2 (CIP-0112) is live — see token_standard_v2.
key_points: Already Replaced by CIP112 / CIP-0112, ALREADY LIVE ON MAINNET.
Token Metadata: name, symbol, totalSupply
Holdings: portfolio view from validator node
Transfer Instruction: FOP peer-to-peer transfers
Allocation: DVP atomic settlement
All amounts use Daml Decimal (10 decimal places)
No unconstrained allowances — allocations cover this
CC supports 24h signing/submission delays for token standard transfers and allocations (CIP-0107, Splice 0.5.16)
Scan choice context must be passed through opaquely
Token metadata API has accountInputFieldsToShow to tell wallets whether an instrument uses account-ids or account providers (Splice 0.6.12)

token_standard_v2.title: Token Standard V2 (CIP-0112)
token_standard_v2.summary: Improvements for privacy, performance and traditional accounting. Released in Splice 0.6.11 with a full Amulet (CC) implementation. CIP112 / CIP-0112 IS ALREADY LIVE ON MAINNET.
key_points: Tokens supporting V2 MUST implement both the Daml interfaces and the OpenAPI specs; they may implement allocation, transfer, or both
Committed allocations: funds locked until the settlement deadline
Iterated allocations: executor sets the actual amount at settlement, as long as allocated funds cover it
Allocations for burn (prepares paying for CNS entries, traffic, etc. via allocations)
Single-step transfers through the V2 transfer factory when sender and receiver authorization are both available
Transaction history: all holding changes reported as V2 EventLog_HoldingsChange events — much simpler parsing for wallets/explorers
Accounts: support for rich account structures common in TradFi
AmuletConfig.tokenStandardMaxTTL (default 90 days) caps lifetime of transfer instructions and allocations; DSO can expire older ones
splice-util-token-standard-wallet.dar adds BatchingUtilityV2 to batch V1/V2 actions in one transaction; uploaded and vetted by default on validators
Splice Amulet Wallet UI supports V2 but does not create all requested allocations in one transaction (Amulet-only limitation)
Validator 0.8.3 fixed the Scan proxy missing V2 allocation-instruction and transfer-instruction endpoints
Definitions: https://github.com/canton-network/splice/tree/main/token-standard ; DARs: https://github.com/canton-network/splice/tree/main/daml/dars

splice_packages.title: Splice Package Architecture
splice_packages.summary: Seven Daml packages for CC, CNS, and governance.
key_points: splice-util, splice-amulet (CC), splice-amulet-name-service (CNS)
splice-dso-governance, splice-validator-lifecycle
splice-wallet-payments (subscription deprecated), splice-wallet (being replaced by token standard)
Use Daml interfaces for decoupling from Splice upgrades
Apps that statically depend on splice-amulet must recompile when AmuletConfig changes (latest: amulet 0.1.23 in Splice 0.8.0). Depending only on token standard interfaces avoids this.
Current package versions (Splice 0.8.0+): amulet 0.1.23, amuletNameService 0.1.24, dsoGovernance 0.1.29, validatorLifecycle 0.1.9, wallet 0.1.24, walletPayments 0.1.23
Unsupported splice DAR versions are automatically unvetted by SVs and (since 0.6.13) by validators

featured_apps.title: Featured App Rewards
featured_apps.summary: Featured apps earn CC rewards. The original model (CIP-0047) used FeaturedAppActivityMarker contracts; it is being replaced by traffic-based app rewards (CIP-0104).
key_points: Apply via tokenomics committee
CIP-0047 model: create FeaturedAppActivityMarker for important events (~$1 USD/marker); per-transaction app rewards capped at $1.50 (CIP-0098)
Markers can be weighted (FeaturedAppRight weight, CIP-0104 amendment); weights only per tokenomics committee guidance
Once traffic-based app rewards are enabled on a network, CC transfers stop creating markers — see traffic_based_app_rewards

Splice 0.8.0: Scan no longer adds featured-app-right to choice context (after SV switchover). To feature a CC transfer, fetch /api/scan/v0/featured-apps/{provider_party_id} and add it under 'featured-app-right'
Featured App Staking framework: CIP-0116
Self-feature on DevNet for testing
WalletUserProxy helps wallet providers earn rewards

traffic_based_app_rewards.title: Traffic-Based App Rewards (CIP-0104)
traffic_based_app_rewards.summary: App rewards computed by SV apps off-ledger from the traffic transactions actually burn, replacing activity markers. Rolled out incrementally (Splice 0.5.11 → 0.7.x). Check the network's AmuletConfig.rewardConfig to see whether it is live or in dry-run.
key_points: Increment 1: confirmation responses made free (Splice 0.5.11)
Scan /v0/events and /v0/events/{update_id} return traffic_summary and app_activity_records per transaction — use them to preview expected rewards
Rewards depend on your exact transaction structure and on the featured status of counterparties, so DevNet/TestNet/MainNet can differ
Transactions submitted by SVs do not generate app activity
RewardCouponV2: created in batches once per round per eligible party; time-based expiry, mintable up to ~36h after creation so beneficiaries can batch minting
Mint via Splice Wallet automation (internal parties, or external parties with a MintingDelegation) or directly with AmuletRules_Transfer
splice-api-reward-assignment-v1 lets decentralized apps assign rewards to ultimate beneficiaries
reward-sharing-config-by-party type=external lets your own process assign/mint coupons (Splice 0.7.1)
App activity records and traffic ingestion are always on in Scan since Splice 0.7.4
Validator-side follow-up: CIP-0120 Traffic-Based Validator Rewards (Proposed)

development_fund.title: Canton Development Fund (CIP-0082 / CIP-0100)
development_fund.summary: 5% of each Canton Coin mint goes to a Foundation-governed Development Fund (CIP-0082), governed per CIP-0100. Builders apply via PRs to the canton-dev-fund GitHub repo.
key_points: On-ledger: UnclaimedDevelopmentFundCoupon accrues per round; the Development Fund Manager allocates DevelopmentFundCoupon to beneficiaries, who mint them via AmuletRules_Transfer
Wallet UI /development-fund page: fund total, allocation form (manager), coupon history (beneficiaries can view, not withdraw)

Splice 0.8.0: optional mintAfter on DevelopmentFundCoupon; SVs can set minDevelopmentFundMintingDelay and developmentFundManagerBlacklist (Quantstamp audit QS2). Once a non-zero delay is set, AmuletRules_AllocateDevelopmentFundCoupon calls without mintAfter are rejected
Two proposal paths: RFP-aligned (rfps/<category>/) or individual initiative (proposals/)

Before submitting: read the 2026–2028 strategic roadmap and RFPs, discuss with the relevant SIG, gather evidence of need, find a Development Fund Champion, use the current template, follow the AI policy

Five RFP categories: developer-experience-tooling-education, financial-markets-standards-verification, governance-identity-network-coordination, protocol-infrastructure-scalability-resilience, security-assurance-incident-readiness
Approved/merged proposals: go to https://github.com/canton-foundation/canton-dev-fund/tree/main/proposals — every file there on main is an approved proposal. Never rely on a hardcoded list.

Need a validator node (self-host or node-as-a-service)
Wallets safekeep DATA and assets — preserving customer privacy

Point-in-time or latest-available basis
Filter by party and contract template
JSONB columns — create custom indexes for optimization
Crash-tolerant, restartable safely
Security: only canReadAs/readAsAnyParty needed — no actAs/admin

minTopupAmount: minimum purchase to amortize SV processing cost

FAQ.question: What is CIP-0103?
FAQ.answer:
CIP-0103 is the Canton dApp standard — defines how wallets and dApps connect and interoperate. Analogous to WalletConnect/EIP-1193 on Ethereum.

Two sides:
- Wallets implement the dApp API (server-side or browser extension)
- dApps use the dApp SDK + embed the Discovery Component

Result: any compliant wallet works with any compliant dApp automatically. No bespoke per-pair integration.

Solves the N×M problem: without it, N wallets × M dApps = N×M custom integrations.

Key Canton difference: connection includes party identity + validator node context (not just an address).

Spec: https://github.com/canton-foundation/cips/blob/main/cip-0103/cip-0103.md

FAQ.question: Does Canton has Any Bridge like LayerZero or Wormhole?
FAQ.answer: LayerZero the first interoperability protocol to deploy to Canton, Users can fund primary purchases of Canton-based assets using stablecoins from external public blockchains, tapping Canton's configurable privacy. Similarly, asset issuers can permit tokenized assets – treasuries, bonds, etc – issued on Canton to move across 165+ blockchains for secondary market trading.

FAQ.question: What is the Wallet Gateway?
FAQ.answer:
Wallet Gateway is deployed in your own environment, adjacent to your validator node. It bridges your validator to an external custody/signing provider so private keys never need to live on the validator.

Supports: Fireblocks, BitGo, DFNS, Blockdaemon (and others via signing driver abstraction).

Use case: institutions that self-host a Canton validator but manage keys in their existing custody infrastructure.

Flow:
1. dApp requests signing via CIP-0103
2. Wallet Gateway intercepts
3. Routes to custody provider via signing driver
4. Gets signature back
5. Submits transaction — keys never left the custody provider

Source: Digital Asset Wallet Unit.

FAQ.question: What is the Discovery Component?
FAQ.answer:
A drop-in TypeScript UI component for dApp developers. Embed it in your dApp frontend and users see a list of all CIP-0103 compliant wallets they can connect — like RainbowKit on Ethereum.

Always pair with the dApp SDK (the component is UI; the SDK is the protocol layer).

Network effect: every new wallet that implements CIP-0103 automatically appears in the discovery component — existing dApps get new wallet support for free without code changes.

Source: Digital Asset Wallet Unit.

FAQ.question: What is the Reference Wallet?
FAQ.answer:
An open-source, production-ready browser extension wallet for Canton. Real key management, real signing, CIP-0103 compliant.

Important: does NOT bundle validator access. Users still need their own Canton validator node (self-hosted or via NaaS) to use the network. The Reference Wallet provides only the wallet layer.

Three strategic purposes:
1. Dogfoods DA's own SDKs/standards (if broken, the SDK is broken)
2. Gives external wallet teams a production-grade reference to build from
3. Covers functionality commercial wallets may skip (e.g. key recovery flow)

Available as a GitHub repo for download and self-deployment.

Source: Digital Asset Wallet Unit.

FAQ.question: What is the Portfolio UI?
FAQ.answer:
Open-source reference dApp for viewing and managing Canton assets. NOT a wallet — no key management or signing.

Users: clone it, install, connect any CIP-0103 compliant wallet, and use it as a portfolio dashboard.

Capabilities: view holdings, initiate transfers/offers/allocations, multi-party views, supports Wallet Gateway setups.

Expected to replace the splice amulet wallet UI that currently ships bundled with validator tooling.

Source: Digital Asset Wallet Unit.

FAQ.question: What is the Wallet SDK?
FAQ.answer:
TypeScript SDK from DA Wallet Unit for institutions, exchanges, and custodians integrating with Canton.

Wraps the low-level Ledger API and exposes clean methods for:
- Creating parties
- Preparing and submitting transactions
- Handling delegations
- Querying balances and holdings
- CIP-0056 token standard workflows

Target users: wallet developers (Loop, Bron, Ledger-type builds), exchanges, custodians, NaaS providers.

Purpose: every integrator shouldn't build their own Ledger API plumbing from scratch.

Source: Digital Asset Wallet Unit.

FAQ.question: Which Wallet Unit product do I need?
FAQ.answer:
Building a wallet or custody integration? → Wallet SDK
Running your own validator + external custody (Fireblocks/BitGo/DFNS)? → Wallet Gateway
Building a dApp that needs wallet connectivity? → dApp SDK + Discovery Component (always both)
Need a reference/open-source wallet? → Reference Wallet
Need a portfolio/asset dashboard dApp? → Portfolio UI

All products connect via CIP-0103 — the shared interoperability standard.

Source: Digital Asset Wallet Unit.

FAQ.answer:

JSON: dpm damlc inspect-dar --json myfile.dar (main_package_id = package hash)

FAQ.question: Canton vs Ethereum?
FAQ.answer: Selective visibility (no global state), party-as-vault, UTXO model, two-phase commit, Daml (not Solidity). Synchronizer can't read transaction data. Complementary to public blockchains — institutional privacy use cases.

FAQ.question: How do I transfer tokens?
FAQ.answer:
Token Standard (CIP-0056, V2 in CIP-0112):
1. TransferPreapproval: receiver preapproves (1-step deposits); base 90 days free (CIP-0119)
2. Transfer Instruction API: FOP transfers
3. Allocation API: DVP settlement (V2 adds committed and iterated allocations)

CC transfers have NO fees (CIP-0078) and support 24h submission delays (CIP-0107).
The old TransferCommand API was removed in Splice 0.8.0.
Docs: https://docs.canton.network/appdev/deep-dives/token-standard#token-standard

FAQ.answer: Shared Reth-based EVM on Canton. EVM payloads wrap into Canton transactions atomically. NOT an L2 rollup. Uses external_call() Daml primitive. Built by Zenith.

FAQ.answer: Local sandbox: no auth. Production: JWT (RS256). Splice apps: sub=ledger-api-user, aud=configured audience. OAuth2 Authorization Code for UIs. Configure OIDC provider (Auth0, Keycloak).

FAQ.question: Featured application?
FAQ.answer:

2. Rewards are moving from activity markers (CIP-0047, ~$1/marker, capped at $1.50 per tx by CIP-0098) to traffic-based app rewards (CIP-0104), where rewards follow the traffic your transactions burn
3. Preview your expected rewards via Scan /v0/events app_activity_records

FAQ.question: Signatories and observers?
FAQ.answer:
Signatories: required to create/archive. signatory keyword. Every contract needs one. See creation+archival.
Observers: can see, can't act. observer keyword. See create/archive.
Controllers: can exercise a choice. controller keyword. Required authorizers.

FAQ.question: Propose-accept pattern?
FAQ.answer: Most common multi-party pattern. Party A creates Proposal (A=signatory). Party B exercises Accept (adds B's authority). Creates final contract with both signatories. Standard triple: Accept/Reject/Cancel.

FAQ.question: What is PQS?
FAQ.answer:
Participant Query Store — SQL read layer for Canton. Ingests ledger data into PostgreSQL.

Install: dpm install <version> (includes scribe.jar)
Locate jar: dpm resolve | grep scribe
Docker: europe-docker.pkg.dev/da-images/public/docker/participant-query-store:<version>

Basic usage:
./scribe.jar pipeline ledger postgres-document \
  --pipeline-filter-parties 'Alice::*' \
  --pipeline-ledger-start Latest \
  --source-ledger-host canton-host --source-ledger-port 6865 \
  --target-postgres-host pg-host --target-postgres-database mydb

Requires: JDK 17+, PostgreSQL 17 recommended (14 is EOL 2026-11-12). Needs 4GB RAM (PQS) + 8GB RAM (PostgreSQL).
Docs: https://docs.canton.network/sdks-tools/development-tools/pqs

FAQ.question: What is Token Standard V2?
FAQ.answer:
CIP-0112, live since Splice 0.6.11. Adds committed allocations (funds locked until settlement deadline), iterated allocations (executor sets the final amount at settlement), allocations for burn, single-step transfers, accounts for TradFi-style structures, and V2 EventLog_HoldingsChange history events that make parsing much simpler.

Registries must implement both the Daml interfaces and the OpenAPI specs (allocation, transfer, or both). Wallets should add V2 allocation and account support.

FAQ.question: What is CantonBFT?
FAQ.answer:
CantonBFT (formerly DA BFT) is Canton's parallel, multi-leader BFT ordering service. It replaces single-leader CometBFT for higher throughput and better resilience to slow or faulty peers.

- GA for private synchronizers since Canton 3.5.15
- Global Synchronizer switch prepared in Splice 0.8.0, executed via an LSU; done on DevNet, TestNet/MainNet timing to be announced

canton builder start
canton builder deploy ./.daml/dist/your-project-0.0.1.dar

FAQ.question: How do I plug my own Daml project into cn-quickstart?
FAQ.answer:
Follow https://guide.canton.foundation/localnet (Part B). In short:
1. git clone cn-quickstart, cd quickstart, make setup (OAuth2: y)
2. Add your project under quickstart/daml/your-project/ and match sdk-version to DAML_SDK_VERSION in .env
3. Add it to quickstart/daml/multi-package.yaml, then make build
4. make start (and make capture-logs in another terminal)
5. Get a Keycloak token, POST your DAR to http://localhost:3975/v2/packages (and 2975 for app-user)
6. Find party IDs via GET /v2/parties, create contracts via /v2/commands/submit-and-wait
Reset with make stop && make clean-all.
